#3183. NFL On The Future Of Netflix’s Thanksgiving Eve Game & Starting A New Tradition: “We Are Committed”

Netflix is launching a new annual NFL tradition: the first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game. The inaugural game will see the Los Angeles Rams and the Green Bay Packers face off a day before the Thanksgiving Day tripleheader, giving fans more football to enjoy with friends and family during the holiday season.

Grace Senko, NFL Vice President, Media Strategy and Business Development, recently told Deadline how this special game came to be.

“As part of our scheduling process every year, the team takes a look at the upcoming year and looks at potential windows and thinks about how we can continue to innovate the schedule, try new things that we’ve never done before,” Senko said. “[Last year] when we played Christmas on a Wednesday, that was the first time, and then now it’s become kind of a staple throughout the season.”

She continued, “When we think about Thanksgiving Eve, I don’t think we think about Thanksgiving as just being one day. At least I know it feels like everybody in New York has already left a little bit. But for a lot of people, it begins on that Wednesday, already gathering with friends and family, and that kind of extends through Sunday.” Watch on Deadline

Senko notes that the Thanksgiving Day games “continued to perform really strong and really well” last year, adding that they averaged 45M viewers “and was the fourth consecutive year of viewership growth.”

“When you see that, and then you pair that with the Black Friday game that Amazon began distributing in 2023, and the really strong growth over the last few years there, it really made us question: you know, should we be doing something on Thanksgiving Eve? Is there a special moment that we can create there as well, and really, you know, continue to kind of build and expand upon the temple that we’ve already established with Thanksgiving Day?” she added.

Senko says that the game is “an extension of the Thanksgiving Day holiday” and “a unique opportunity that we had in our schedule,” adding, “We are committed to play on Thanksgiving Eve through the duration of our deal with Netflix.”

The Thanksgiving Eve Halftime show will feature U2 amid their 50th anniversary celebration tour. Senko goes back to the Christmas Day game in 2024, which was dubbed Beyoncé Bowl as the singer performed during Halftime, adding, “I think Netflix, at kind of the core of entertainment and culture in our country, is focused on making it as big of a possible moment and event as they possibly can.

Netflix is set to bring the Thanksgiving Eve game back in 2027 as part of their deal with the NFL. This game could potentially be the start of a new tradition for many decades to come.

“We’ll look at this year, but then over time we’ll look at the audience growth,” Senko said about the future of the Thanksgiving Eve game. “We’ll look at feedback from our partners. We’ll get feedback from the clubs, feedback from the various constituents in the organization, and evaluate if it’s a day and an event that we want to continue building. So that’s definitely there. There’s a lot of conversations that will be had, but a lot of different things that we’ll look at, whether evaluating this game or any other window that we’re playing in. That’s kind of new and a non-traditional window, I would say.”

Netflix’s Thanksgiving Eve game streams on Wednesday, November 25, starting at 8 p.m. ET / 5 p.m. PT and will feature U2 during the halftime show.

#3180. The Latest Apple Watch Is Up to $100 Off for Black Friday

Apple's latest flagship smartwatch, the Apple Watch Series 12, is worth the upgrade. With this model, Apple has upgraded the processor, added a new heart rate sensor, and improved the display durability. It's certainly one of Apple's best smartwatches, but that also means it isn't cheap: All these new features give the new Series 12 a starting price of $399, which only increases if you choose a model with cellular data. However, for Black Friday, you can take up to $100 off the Series 12, bringing the starting price down to $299.

The three biggest hardware upgrades with the Apple Watch Series 12 are the heart rate sensor, the S11 chip, and Ceramic Shield 2. That heart rate sensor now checks your pulse every five seconds, or 20 times a minute. Apple says the Series 12 checks your heart rate variability 24 times more than the Series 11, and your background heart rate 60 times more frequently than the Series 11. The company is even so bold as to say the Series 12 has the most accurate heart rate monitor on a wearable.

Powering the new heart rate monitor is the S11 chip, Apple's latest processor for the Apple Watch. The S11 isn't only responsible for these new heart rate features, however. In addition to running the same watchOS 27 features as other compatible Apple Watches, the S11 on the Series 12 can run Audio Intelligence, Apple's new suite of AI-powered audio features. That includes "Live Rewind," which lets you see a transcript of the last 15 seconds of an in-person conversation, and "Siri Recaps," which displays summaries of your conversations throughout the day. Finally, the other major advantage with the Series 12 is Ceramic Shield 2. This is a display upgrade that Apple typically reserves for more premium Apple Watch finishes, but this year, the aluminum Series 12 gets it as well. That means the watch should be more durable against scratches and cracks, without you having to upgrade to the more expensive model.

How much you'll save on a Series 12 depends on the size, color, and model. At this time, Amazon is selling certain colors of the 42mm Series 12 for $299, while certain colors of the 46mm option run $449 (also marked down by $100). You can also save on the cellular models as well: The 42mm option is currently $429 (down from $499), while the 46mm model is $449 (down from $549).

#3179. MagSafe Monday: Anker’s MagGo Pro 2 has a built-in fan to keep 25W Qi2.2 charging from slowing down

The biggest issue with Qi 2.2 on MagSafe batteries is the slowdown caused by heat. It doesn’t matter if the battery specs say it can charge at Qi2.2 speeds if the heat slows it down after 15 minutes. The Anker MagGo 2 Pro directly targets heat with a built-in fan in the MagSafe battery.

MagSafe Monday: Every Monday, Bradley Chambers looks at the latest and greatest in the MagSafe and wireless charging industry to help you get the most out of your Apple devices that support wireless charging.

Heat is the enemy of MagSafe charging, which is why it slows to a crawl on a hot day and why most MagSafe batteries can’t hold their top speed for an entire charge. Anker’s answer in the MagGo 2 Pro is a small fan inside of it. Anker says it keeps the charging surface below 96.8°F, and the fan adjusts its speed based on what’s plugged in and how the charge is progressing. You can switch between Cool and Silent modes if you don’t want to hear it running at all.

The result of having this fan is a Qi2.2 power bank that actually reaches Qi2.2 speeds for a full charge. Anker rates it at 25% on an iPhone 17 Pro in 10 minutes, then to 50% in 25 minutes, which is the kind of speed you’d normally expect from a wired charging session.

The MagGo 2 Pro battery is 10,000mAh, which is enough for a little over one full charge of an iPhone Pro Max and closer to two on a standard iPhone. Size-wise, it has about the same footprint as the iPhone itself and is roughly an ounce lighter than Anker’s standard MagGo. It’s not a slim battery, but for one with a fan, it’s workable in your travel bag, crossbody, etc.

The single USB-C port works both directions at up to 45 watts. If you plug in a 45-watt charger to it, the MagGo 2 Pro can charge from empty to 80% in under an hour. The same port will charge a Mac or an iPad up to 45 watts in a pinch, which is a nice add-on for a MagSafe battery. You are not going to charge up your MacBook Pro from zero to full with it, but it’s a nice way to get a little charge in an emergency at the airport, etc.

One thing to know before you buy: the cable in the box is a 1-foot USB-C-to-USB-C cable, and Anker says that reaching the full 45-watt recharge speed requires a 45-watt-rated cable. So keep that in mind as you pack for a trip.

Anker put a small display on the side that cycles through six screens with a side button: charging wattage, battery percentage, battery health, and temperature. It’s a nice touch to know you are reaching the 25-watt Qi 2.2 speed.

There’s also a built-in stand that adjusts from flat to 80 degrees and folds back into the body when you’re done. You can also quickly turn off charging if you simply want to use it as a stand. The Anker MagGo 2 Pro comes in Phantom Gray, Burgundy Red, Polar Night Blue, and Starlight Silver.

Qi2.2 is the Holy Grail of MagSafe chargers, but as I said in the beginning, it’s irrelevant if the heat throttles it. To get full 25-watt MagSafe charging on the go, you’ll likely need something with a fan, unless you’re in colder weather. The Anker MagGo 2 Pro solves that problem with a built-in fan, a handy side display, and a stand.

The Anker MagGo 2 Pro is available on Amazon and directly from Anker.

#3178. Breaking Baz: ‘Bunker’ Writer-Director Florian Zeller Takes Us Behind The Scenes With Penélope Cruz, Javier Bardem, Stephen Graham & Dame Eileen Atkins

Speaking over Zoom from his home in Paris, Florian Zeller says he could write poems all about Penélope Cruz. Instead, he wrote a thrilling movie called Bunker for her, and her husband, Javier Bardem.

Zeller, the playwright, screenwriter and screen and stage director behind The Father (for which Anthony Hopkins won his second Best Actor Oscar) and plays that have run on Broadway and in London’s West End, emphasizes that he wasn’t interested in Cruz’s radiant beauty. “Of course she’s beautiful,” he says, but, “somehow we don’t care.”

What do you mean? I ask. Related Stories Trailers 'Bunker' Trailer: Penélope Cruz & Javier Bardem Clash In Florian Zeller's Venice Breakout; UK Release Date Set News Netflix Unveils Penélope Cruz & Juan Diego Botto's Domestic Violence Drama 'Patricia' As Production Gets Underway

“Of course, she is talented, but she has something more, something unique, and it has to do with the fact that she’s always working with who she is. She’s always working with her deep emotions, and that in my experience is really rare.” Watch on Deadline

We both extol the three performances Cruz appears in this season. First, his Bunker, of course, in which she plays Sofía, an accomplished editor of foreign fiction at an upscale London publishing house. Bardem plays Miguel, her husband, an eminent architect, who’s handy in the kitchen and adores preparing the family’s meals. In addition, in the Los Javis-directed La Bola Negra, Cruz plays Nené Romero, a cupletista, who performs bawdy songs for troops during the Spanish Civil War. Then in Olivia Wilde’s chamber comedy The Invite, she shows off her comedic chops in the role of Piña, one half of a couple with an experimental approach to partnership.

But it’s Bunker that gives Cruz a lead role and center stage.

As to how Zeller connected with Cruz and Bardem he explains that he had a meeting with Cruz four years ago “but the project was not the right one.” Then, one day, Bardem rang him and marveled over Zeller’s plays and films, saying that he’d screened The Father countless times to study Anthony Hopkins’s performance, to understand how he did it. A little while later, they were both in Los Angeles and Bardem visited Zeller and spent an afternoon in his LA garden “talking about life.” That’s when Zeller shared his desire to write something for both Bardem and Cruz.

Zeller says now that part of his motivation was because they are “such an iconic couple then reality would go almost against fiction, and so I thought it would be much more interesting, challenging, and beautiful to have layers to every scene and to blur the line between fiction and reality.” As with Nicole Kidman and Tom Cruise in Stanley Kubrick’s Eyes Wide Shut and Mike Nichols’s screen version of Edward Albee’s seminal play Who’s Afraid of Virginia Wolf? with Elizabeth Taylor and Richard Burton, we’re fascinated when reality meets fiction, or vice-versa, but it’s not, as Zeller puts it, “to put ourselves in a position of voyeurism.”

(By the way, there’s a fabulous revival of Albee’s Who’s Afraid of Virginia Wolf? on now at @sohoplace Theatre in London’s West End starring Gillian Anderson and Billy Crudup directed by Marianne Elliott.)

Sofía and Miguel have been married for 16 years, just like Cruz and Bardem. The fictional couple in Bunker seem happy at first, but you sense in Sofía that there’s a growing distance. There’s a brilliant opening scene where Sofía and Miguel are dining with friends and Miguel begins to tell fellow guests the story of how they met. However, the camera’s real focus is on Cruz’s face. She’s just listening and says nothing in that moment. “You can feel everything that she is feeling,” says Zeller, “and only the greatest actress can do that with almost no words to say and to express so many things, so many layers. And that’s what I love about that scene. Her face is like a landscape. You know, looking at her to see the how intense, complex, and rich she can be in this quieter, more contained exploration of who she is — that’s something of a new journey of performance.”

Zeller observes that he and Cruz talked a lot about that opening scene, “and the fact that it was about not what she says but what she keeps for herself, and because in the film we feel that she’s going through a crisis without knowing exactly what it is. In another scene she is in front of this painting. Suddenly, she feels melancholy, but we don’t know exactly why. She’s not happy with her life without knowing exactly why…You know, she has a beautiful house, she has a beautiful husband, she has beautiful children, and still, she is unhappy. She doesn’t have the words to describe why she feels that way. What is this melancholy? So, it’s not until the moment comes when there’s this long confrontation and this long argument with Javier, when suddenly she can articulate her thoughts and her feelings. But until then, and it was the challenge for her as an actress, it was to make us understand everything that she’s going through without being able to express it.” Zeller says that “everything that matters was behind the dialogue” and that Cruz’s “silent intensity” blew him away. Me too.

Zeller continues, “You know, I’ve been lucky enough to work with so many great actors, and I can say that she’s really extraordinary to work with. She’s extraordinary, versatile, but always truthful, always intense. She’s never cheating. You know, every emotion she is exploring is coming from a true place, and I think that’s why she’s so special in this industry now…It’s really rare.”

Of Bardem, Zeller observes that he usually plays “very powerful men, very masculine, frightening sometimes, sometimes really scary, and when I met him, I was touched by the fact that he’s such a sensitive, such a delicate, and I would say, almost such a feminine man. And that’s what I wanted to explore in this film. Not to say that this is his story. Of course, that’s not his story and that’s not her story. But what I was really interested in was to try to still leave room for who they are in this film. But what you feel about this character is at least what I feel about who he is as a man, this very delicate way of seeing the world and trying always to leave room for the other. You know he has such a delicacy towards Penélope, for example, and so I feel like it’s almost them, even though it’s characters.”

It’s true that the fear is at the core of the film, and because I think that it’s one of the feelings that really defines the world we are in at the moment. It all started, as you might know, with an article that I read about this tech billionaire building a bunker.

Zeller ensured that they read the script several times “to be aware of what would be the exposure,” and calls the couple “very brave as artists.” As soon as they made the decision to do it, they expressed no fear “to be seen the way they wouldn’t want to be seen.” Their commitment,” he adds, had to do with “the trust, of course,” but also, “with the feeling of being safe. It’s true on set but it’s true in every professional situation that you are a better version of yourself when you feel safe, and as an actor, you feel safe when you feel loved. So, part of my job was to love them or to make them feel loved, and it was not that hard because I truly loved them,” he says.

I ask Zeller to talk about the film’s gripping 12-minute fight scene between the couple, that took three days to shoot. He noticed that Cruz “was really nervous about it, days and days ahead of it.” And when it came time to shoot, Cruz had to be “very mad,” so Bardem “was saying off-camera things that would make her mad.” He laughs. “Javier knew which buttons to push.” Zeller remembers Bardem telling him one day that there was no need to rehearse the couple arguing because they knew how to do that, and in any case not rehearsing that scene would save the production money, a point that Zeller, as a producer of the film, acknowledged.

In bringing Graham on board as the neighbor, Zeller says he admired the actor’s performance in Netflix hit, Adolescence, but for Bunker he was looking for an actor “that was capable of putting Bardem at risk. It’s not that easy because usually Javier Bardem is the one to threaten everybody else. And for some reason, Stephen Graham has this menacing presence.” But he was also struck by Graham’s ability “to have something so human.” It’s a small but integral part and Zeller was struck by Graham’s humility. Zeller says, “When he read the script, he said, ‘OK, it’s not a big role, but I know exactly what I can do with that. I know exactly why I want to do it.’”

“It’s not a conscious reference, because that play is not clear in my mind,” says Zeller, “but it’s true that the fear is at the core of the film, and because I think that it’s one of the feelings that really defines the world we are in at the moment. It all started, as you might know, with an article that I read about this tech billionaire building a bunker.” When I suggest that Zeller and I must’ve read the same article in the New York Times about Mark Zuckerberg and his bunker, Zeller responds, “Exactly.”

He was, he says, struck by the idea that this man “who made a fortune from the idea of connecting people together was working at the same time on a plan B to isolate himself.” That’s what gave him the impetus to write the film. “It’s such a strange position in life to have to work on something that would mean that maybe soon it’s the end of the world. The more I was thinking about it, the more I realized that, to some degree, we are all tempted to live in a bunker,” he says. He clarifies, “like an invisible bunker to build things to feel protected, without realizing that it’s another kind of prison.”

Zeller worries that we are all adopting the lifestyle “that these billionaires are promoting, it is a world of illusions where you almost believe that you don’t really need the others. You know, like everything could be delivered to you, like food, love, friendship, social interactions, cinema, as if the world out there was not a place to explore anymore. As if we were like isolated islands and not interconnected continents.”

Speaking of “interconnections,” there’s a reconnection of sorts in Bunker. Several years ago, Zeller penned the West End and Broadway play The Height of the Storm which starred Dame Eileen Atkins and theatrical knight Jonathan Pryce. During pre-production on Bunker, Zeller approached Dame Atkins to ask if she’d take a cameo role of a woman who meets Cruz’s character in a powder room and offers her some sage advice. It’s just a moment on screen, but it holds enormous symbolism, that of one great artist passing the baton to another.

Zeller nods in agreement and speaks of his “respect and admiration” for the classically-trained Atkins, now in her 93rd year. The grande dame had told Zeller that she was retired. So, while the interiors were being shot in Madrid to allow Cruz and Bardem to be close to their children, Zeller was so keen to have Atkins in his film that he offered to shoot the scene in London.

What followed was “a very moving moment” because it was the last scene shot in the film, “so it was the wrap for Penelope and for her, and it was really emotional because the scene is very short and it’s basically her saying, ‘You’re so beautiful, and you should enjoy it because you know things are going very, very fast, faster than what you think,’ which is a very simple and common thought. But that’s also the truth. Not only a character saying that to another character, but it was also a woman of a certain age saying that to Penélope, and it was also an older actress that had stopped working saying that to another actress. So, it was so many layers of transmission between two women. I mean, they both cried at the end, and then, it was so moving, Eileen said, ‘Oh, that was my very last apparition on the screen.’”

Sony Pictures Classics opens Bunker in select U.S. cities on December 11 and then nationwide on January 15, 2027.

StudioCanal will release the film in the U.K. and Ireland on February 19.

#3177. If You Loved 'The Good Daughter,' There's One Movie You Need to Watch Next

Jeff Somers is a freelancer who has been writing about writing, books, personal finance, and home maintenance since 2012.

Jeff has published nine novels and more than 70 short stories; his story Ringing the Changes was selected for inclusion in The Best American Mystery Stories 2006. In 2018, Jeff published the book Writing Without Rules: How to Write & Sell a Novel Without Guidelines, Experts, or (Occasionally) Pants. He holds a bachelor’s degree in English and previously worked in medical publishing as a production editor.

When not writing, Jeff spends his free time fixing up his old house. He has tackled a wide range of DIY projects, including remodeling a bathroom entirely on his own in two weeks, and building a roof deck that hasn't fallen down yet. You can find him on Bluesky.

This is Streamalikes, where you can find a curated list of recommendations to stream based on what you already like.

There are plenty of reasons Peacock’s The Good Daughter is so damn watchable. The performances, for one—Rose Byrne and Meghann Fahy are terrific as estranged sisters Sam and Charlotte Quinn. But it’s also a great story, tracing the corrosive effect of a years-ago trauma on the women and their lawyer father (Brendan Gleeson) amid the slow revelation of many extremely dark secrets. If you want more of that flavor of trauma-driven drama with a tight focus on family bonds, there’s one movie you should watch: 2015's Dark Places.

You want buried secrets? Dark Places has seriously buried secrets. Adapted from the Gillian Flynn novel, the film follows Libby Day (Charlize Theron), who survived the mass murder of her family in 1985. The crime is blamed on her brother Ben, a moody loner whose conviction was based in large part on Libby’s own testimony. For a long time, Libby is financially sustained by donations from people who sympathize with her plight, but three decades after the murders, the money has dried up, and Libby is desperate—so desperate, she agrees to help out a “true crime” club that believes her brother is innocent and is working toward his release.

Like The Good Daughter, Dark Places is anchored by a sibling relationship reshaped by the impact of horrifying violence. Libby and Ben’s experience mirrors Sam and Charlie’s in many ways, including in the way both Libby and Ben carry secrets for years after the terrible events that took family from them. The stories are also both compelling mysteries, slowly revealing the shocking truths behind one horrific night, and ultimately allowing the characters to better understand one another.

Dark Places also explores the insular, suffocating nature of small-town life, and how rumor and gossip become a poisonous presence in people’s lives. Libby, Ben, Sam, and Charlie all have to deal with others' assumptions and revelations that they've been betrayed by those closest to them, leading to powerful resolutions. If you loved The Good Daughter, you’ll love this movie. Stream Dark Places on The Roku Channel or Kanopy, or rent it on Prime Video.

Want more stories about family dynamics around secrets, violence, and explosive emotional confrontations? Here are a few more movies fans of The Good Daughter are bound to enjoy.

There’s no violent crime at the heart of this slow-burn drama—just an explosive chaos agent named Kym, played by Anne Hathaway. If your favorite aspect of The Good Daughter was the relationship between sisters Sam and Charlie, then this movie is perfect. Released from rehab to attend her sister’s wedding, Kym is self-hating, angry, and haunted by a terrible event from her childhood. Her sister, Rachel (Rosemary DeWitt), is welcoming, but has never truly forgiven Kym, and the simmering tension between the sisters and the rest of the family drives a drama that you won’t be able to look away from. Stream Rachel Getting Married on Apple TV or rent it on Prime Video.

If you really vibed on the Southern setting, the slow-burn mystery, and the exploration of flawed justice in the modern age depicted in The Good Daughter, check out Where the Crawdads Sing. It’s a slower, dreamier rumination on rural life, violence and its cost, and small-town justice, but it hits the same sweet spot in its story about a woman named Kya (Daisy Edgar-Jones) who was raised in an isolated house in the swamps of North Carolina. Accused in 1969 of a murder, Kya’s story stretches back to her childhood, when she’s slowly abandoned by her entire family, leaving her at age seven to survive on her own. Ostracized as the “swamp girl” by the town, Kya fights to live her life and be loved while facing the unwanted—and violently persistent—attention of the murder victim. It’s about broken families, deeply buried secrets, and what we do to survive. Stream Where the Crawdads Sing on Hulu or rent it on Prime Video.

The Good Daughter is about life in a small, Southern town, family trauma, and the legal system—which makes A Time to Kill the perfect movie to watch when you finish the show. When a Black man’s daughter is sexually assaulted in Mississippi and her attackers—local members of the Ku Klux Klan—look likely to go free, he violently and publicly murders them. Local lawyer Jake Brigance (Matthew McConaughey) takes on the case, assisted by law student Ellen Roark (Sandra Bullock). They face violent opposition, withering racism, and an unfair legal system that echoes the environment in The Good Daughter in ways fans will appreciate. Stream A Time to Kill on YoutTube or rent it on Prime Video.

The Dry might be as close as you can get to The Good Daughter in terms of tone and story. Although set in Australia instead of the American South, The Dry is a story driven by past crimes and buried secrets in a rural setting just like the show. Twenty years ago, Federal agent Aaron Falk (Eric Bana) fled his hometown when he was suspected of the murder of his girlfriend. When his childhood friend, Luke, appears to have murdered his wife and young son before killing himself, he returns to investigate. The slow revelation of two mysteries—one in the past and one simmering in the drought-stricken present—makes this an ideal companion film to the show. Stream The Dry on The Roku Channel, Kanopy, or Tubi, or rent it on Prime Video.

Set in Boston instead of the South, and focused on male friendships instead of a sisters’ bond, Mystic River nevertheless nails the same atmosphere of dread as The Good Daughter. In 1975, boyhood friends Jimmy, Dave, and Sean are traumatized when Dave is abducted and assaulted by two men. In 1990, the three men remain connected in their Boston neighborhood—Jimmy (Sean Penn) is an ex-convict still connected to local crime, Sean (Kevin Bacon) is a State Police detective, and Dave (Tim Robbins) is a blue-collar worker still haunted by his experience. When Jimmy’s daughter is found murdered and Dave seems implicated, Sean and Jimmy launch investigations from either side of the law, with Dave’s fate hanging in the balance. The ending is powerfully brutal, but this story of secrets and suspicion will resonate with fans of the show. Rent Mystic River on Prime Video.

#3174. Aaron Rodgers Released By NFL’s Pittsburgh Steelers Following ESPN Interview Where He Criticized Coach Mike McCarthy After Benching

Aaron Rodgers has been released by the Pittsburgh Steelers following an explosive interview on ESPN‘s Pat McAfee Show.

The Super Bowl champion and 4x NFL MVP was benched this week, and backup quarterback Mason Rudolph was named to take his place in the Black Friday game against the Denver Broncos.

Rodgers, a frequent caller on the sports show, appeared to discuss the situation and, moments later, was confirmed to have been let go by the Steelers.

“I got the day off, so that’s why we’re able to do this,” Rodgers said on the ESPN talk show. Related Stories Sports NFL On The Future Of Netflix's Thanksgiving Eve Game & Starting A New Tradition: "We Are Committed" News Netflix Releases New Peter Berg-Directed Spot Inspired By 'Friday Night Lights' Highlighting Thanksgiving Eve Game

Rodgers said he heard he would be inactive for Amazon’s Prime Video game on Friday from a phone call with other members of the organization, not from Coach Mike McCarthy, whom he had spoken to earlier that day. Watch on Deadline

The football star noted that he had been talking to McCarthy in the last days, but talks about benching were not part of their conversation. Rodgers recalled his interactions with the Steelers coach in the last few days and claimed McCarthy came into a quarterback meeting “late, sat down and within 10 minutes began snoring.”

Rodgers said that after waking himself up again, “five minutes later, you hear the snoring again and less than five minutes after that he walks out of the room like nothing happened.” He added that McCarthy didn’t show up to other meetings and walk-throughs that week.

The quarterback said he had expressed concern over McCarthy’s health, approaching him as a friend, since sleeping during a meeting is a sign someone isn’t healthy.

Later on in the interview, Rodgers suggested that what was best for the team was for McCarthy not to call the plays anymore, adding, “If he wasn’t up for that, then they should probably release me.”

“At this point, I’m not going back to Pittsburgh. That ship has definitely sailed,” he said.

Shortly after his interview on The Pat McAfee Show, reports said Rodgers had been released.

Rodgers signed with the Steelers this season as a swan song and was planning to retire from the NFL at the end of the season. With Rodgers being released, any team can sign him until 4 p.m. ET on Thursday. If he goes unsigned, he would become a free agent.

#3173. Apple Watch SE 3 vs Series 12: Which should you buy this holiday season?

The holiday shopping season is here, and Apple Watch is always a popular gift. Apple’s lineup includes the affordable Apple Watch SE 3 and the more advanced Apple Watch Series 12.

Here’s how those two Apple Watch models stack up…

The Apple Watch SE 3 is the most affordable way to enter the Apple Watch ecosystem. It got a big update last year, adding a variety of new higher-end Apple Watch features. It now offers an Always-On display, sleep apnea notifications, temperature sensing, interactive wrist flick and double tap gestures, and more.

The Apple Watch SE 3 offers 18 hours of battery life, though you can stretch that to 32 hours in Low Power Mode. It supports fast charging, going from 0-80% in 45 minutes.

Even though it hasn’t been updated in a year, the Apple Watch SE 3 is a very compelling option, especially for people new to the Apple Watch ecosystem. It’s pretty fantastic that you can get an Apple Watch with key display and health-monitoring features for under $200.

The Apple Watch Series 12 is Apple’s newest smartwatch, and it’s a big update over its predecessor. This year, Apple doubled down on the health and fitness capabilities of Apple Watch with an all-new Health Sensing System.

Apple touts that the Apple Watch Series 12 delivers “the most accurate heart rate sensing in a wearable.” In fact, the company conducted a study of more than 1,000 participants that found the Series 12 “achieved statistically better overall accuracy than every competing wearable it tested across workouts and daily activities.”

With the new system, Apple Watch Series 12 captures your heart rate every five seconds. Previous Apple Watch models, including the Apple Watch SE 3, take measurements every five minutes. The new Health Sensing System also enables a new readiness score feature, which factors in your recent activity, training load, vitals, and sleep score.

As I wrote in my review, the Apple Watch Series 12 brings some of the biggest improvements to Apple Watch health tracking in years. The new sensing system unlocks a trove of new data along with better accuracy.

The Apple Watch lineup is incredibly strong right now. Whether you’re deciding between the SE 3 and Series 12, both offer great health tracking, battery life, and connectivity. The Apple Watch SE 3 is an excellent choice for people new to the Apple Watch ecosystem.

The Apple Watch Series 12, however, is the best Apple Watch for most people. There are major improvements to the health tracking capabilities, offering meaningful steps forward in what the Apple Watch can tell you about yourself. In the two months I’ve had mine, I’ve come to appreciate the more frequent heart rate measurement and readiness score.

What do you think of the current Apple Watch lineup? Are you shopping for one this holiday season? Let us know down in the comments.

#3171. Anthropic launches new Claude Ship feature for builders

Anthropic is launching a new tool for builders called Claude Ship. The new AI feature allows Claude to “review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones that a team’s policy allows.”

Claude Ship is a new product created especially for builders who code with agents. The idea is to make handling pull requests as automated as agentic coding.

“That’s why we built Claude Ship, available today in beta,” Anthropic says. “It can review PRs, fix them, and decide what’s ready to merge based on policies each team sets. Teams stay in control of where it runs and which changes need a person. The goal: ship code as fast as teams write it.”

Claude Ship is comprised of three agents: Code Review, PR Steward, and Claude Approvals.

“Together, they take a pull request through review, fixes, and an approval decision so teams don’t have to manage each step manually,” Anthropic says.

“Developers can try Claude Ship on their own pull requests with the new /ship command in Claude Code,” Anthropic says.

You can learn much more about Claude Ship here. Additional documentation can be found here.

#3170. Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade Postponed To Saturday Due To Severe Weather; NBC Will Rerun 2025 Parade On Thursday

The Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade will be postponed until Saturday due to expected storms on Thursday.

In a statement, NBC says, “Due to the extreme weather conditions, the city of New York, Macy’s and NBC have decided, in the interest of safety for both the participants and spectators, to move the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday, Nov. 28.

“More details to follow,” the statement continues. “In addition, NBC will telecast the 2025 Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade tomorrow at 8:30 a.m. in all time zones.” Related Stories News NBC Tracking Storm Due To Hit 100th Annual Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade: Will Balloons Be Grounded? News Jack McBrayer To Host NBC's 'Countdown To Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade' Featuring Interviews With Leslie Odom Jr & McKenna Grace

An official announcement is expected shortly. A weather and security briefing from Macy’s officials and the NYPD was planned for 5:30 p.m. ET. Watch on Deadline

As reported by Deadline yesterday, NBC had been closely tracking the Thanksgiving storm expected to bring high winds and heavy rain to New York City and much of the Eastern U.S. The network’s coverage of the 100th edition of the annual Macy’s Thanksgiving Day parade was set to air Thursday on NBC and stream on Peacock from 8:30 a.m. to noon ET.

The parade remains a major draw, with last year’s pulling in 34.3 million viewers across NBC and Peacock, its biggest combined audience on record.

The Nor’easter, a classic storm pattern, is expected to take shape late Wednesday and into Thursday morning, gathering strength as it grinds toward the Atlantic Ocean later in the holiday. Sustained winds are expected to be 12-25 miles an hour with gusts of 20 to 30 mph, increasing over the course of the day. AccuWeather is expecting one to two inches of rain to fall on New York, making this likely to be one of the wettest Thanksgivings in the city’s history.

This year’s parade is especially significant to Macy’s and NBC, as it marks the broadcast’s centennial. The parade is set to have 100 of its trademark large balloons, and a special “All-Star Broadway Thanksgiving Day Celebration” will feature performers from new and long-running Broadway productions in a special 10-minute medley.

The balloons have only been grounded once before, in 1971, due to a similar mix of rain and wind.

During the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, the parade was converted into a television-only event around the Herald Square location of Macy’s Department Store.

That price does still undercut the latest Garmin Fenix 9 line-up, which starts at $999, though some rivals are cheaper still. For instance, the Suunto Vertical 2 steel model costs $599, and the Garmin Fenix 8 is currently on sale for $749.99 at Amazon.

Built-in flashlights have become a must-have feature on premium sports watches, and now the Vertix 4 is the first Coros watch to get one. Coros has departed from the usual layout, though. Garmin, Suunto and Amazfit put the light on top of the watch, but Coros places it on the side, between the digital dial and the back button.

Previous Vertix watches used a memory-in-pixel (MIP) display. MIP has advantages, most notably longer battery life, but I know I much prefer the vibrant display on AMOLED screens, like on the Vertix 4. It is the biggest visual change and a large part of why the watch looks more premium than its predecessors.

Coros claims up to 30 days in watch mode, or 10 days with the screen always on. It also quotes 48 hours of multi-band GPS tracking with the screen always on. I haven't had time to test these claims properly, so stay tuned.

Coros watches are high-quality sports watches, but don't expect to find all the little lifestyle features you've come to expect on a more traditional smartwatch:

Music: It can store tracks, but only files you drag and drop onto the watch. It doesn't pair with streaming services.

Payments: There is no NFC payment support.

Watch faces: Customization is more limited than on rivals.

On paper, the Vertix 4 looks like a significant upgrade: a better display, a more attractive design, a flashlight and satellite maps, at a price well below the Fenix 9 line-up. The $100 increase and cheaper alternatives like the Suunto Vertical 2 and discounted Fenix 8 will matter to some buyers, as will the limited smart features.

#3165. How Microcredentials Can Help Engineers Build Trustworthy AI

IEEE Credentialing Program pairs AI governance standards with microcredentials

Kaitlyn Ridel is the IEEE microcredentials marketing specialist.

Engineering teams are moving at breakneck speed to integrate artificial intelligence, but they are running into a formidable new barrier: compliance issues. Translating high-level AI ethics, governance, and auditing into daily operational workflows has become one of the industry’s toughest challenges.

“AI ethics” refers to the principles developers use to govern and operate workflows. “Governance” refers to the rules and procedures an organization establishes for AI workflows and how they interact with organizational data. Auditing is the process of assessing and validating systems to ensure safety, fairness, transparency, and legal compliance.

Technology leads and systems engineers are responsible for adhering to a structured set of guidelines for standards and processes usually issued by a governing body such as the European Union, the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology, and the International Organization for Standardization.

The regulations aim to mitigate issues such as systemic bias, security vulnerabilities, and transparency risks, but they also highlight a critical skills gap.

Most traditional computer science, software, and electrical engineering degree programs were built around technical design and system architecture. They do not yet include training in AI auditing, data tracking, or safety protocols for how AI systems interact with people and other technologies.

Expecting mid-career engineers to leave their job to attend a full-time two- or four-year program to learn about the topics is not feasible. Yet treating safety and governance as an afterthought can lead to costly product delays, legal exposure, and broken public trust.

Targeted microcredential programs can bridge the knowledge gap by helping engineers build skills in compliance, AI ethics, and governance.

Skills-based microcredentials represent the mastery of expertise gained through a learning program. To earn them, learners must demonstrate the skill through a validation assessment. The microcredentials can be stacked, showing a growing skill set in a defined area and allowing learners to earn several microcredentials in one program.

Microcredentials also allow engineers to upskill and master critical competencies, such as bias mitigation, algorithmic transparency, and risk auditing, without interrupting their career. Through rigorous skills-validation assessments, microcredentials give tech leaders verifiable proof that their teams can audit systems effectively before deployment.

For engineering organizations, microcredentialing creates an agile upskilling pathway. It connects software engineering and hardware design directly to regulatory frameworks, empowering teams to certify systems for safety and compliance within their development life cycles.

Bridging technical capability and ethical responsibility requires a trusted foundation. IEEE has long been a pioneer in socio-technical standards, most notably through the IEEE 7000 series for ethics in AI system design, a framework created to address ethical considerations during the development life cycle.

The IEEE Credentialing Program translates the organization’s world-class standards into actionable, industry-aligned microcredentials. For more than three decades, IEEE has set the gold standard for technical validation and professional certification. By pairing cutting-edge AI governance standards with targeted microcredential programs, IEEE provides engineers and IT leaders with clear, standardized road maps to build systems that are not just technically advanced but also safe, compliant, and worthy of public trust.

To learn more about the credentialing program, explore the offerings or connect with an IEEE expert.

Kaitlyn Ridel is a marketing specialist for the IEEE Microcredentialing Program

#3162. 28 Zero-Day Findings in Under Two Days. Is Robotics Security Keeping Pace?

VicOne’s AI-assisted research reveals what faster zero-day discovery means for robot safety

VicOne is a Physical AI cybersecurity company protecting vehicles and robots from cyber threats that can alter behavior and compromise safety.

VicOne used AI to find 28 zero-day vulnerabilities in Physical AI tools —these weaknesses can impact robot training, testing, and real-world control.

This article is brought to you by VicOne.

VicOne identified an initial set of 28 zero-day findings in less than two days using AI-assisted research across software and tools supporting the Physical AI ecosystem. These include projects developed or maintained by Google, NVIDIA, and Meta, among others.

Based on initial validation, all 28 findings are classified as zero-day vulnerabilities. The count may change following vendor and vulnerability-authority review, and some findings do not yet have CVE tracking numbers.

Many of these tools help teams train, simulate, test, and operate robots. Weaknesses in them could influence the models teams build, the test results they trust, and the instructions sent to robots.

These findings create two demands for robotics teams: responding as AI helps uncover weaknesses faster, and assessing how each one could affect robot safety and operations.

Vulnerability discovery involves examining code, tracing how systems communicate, and testing whether a suspected weakness can actually be exploited. AI can accelerate parts of this work, helping researchers analyze more software in less time. Attackers could use similar capabilities.

When the weakness is a zero-day — previously unknown and without an available fix — faster discovery can leave teams with little time to respond. While that exposure does not necessarily mean an attack has occurred, teams still need to determine whether they use the affected software and what an attacker could access or change.

VicOne’s findings span three stages of the robotics lifecycle: development and training, simulation and validation, and deployment and runtime. Weaknesses at each stage could affect what a robot learns, how it is tested, and how it is controlled.

Figure 1. In this research set, 75% of findings involved development, training, simulation, or validation tools, highlighting risks that can arise before a robot is deployed.VicOne

The following scenarios show how a compromised component could influence the robot at each stage.

These are potential consequences and not demonstrated outcomes for every finding. Actual effects depend on the attacker’s access, the system’s design, and whether other safeguards prevent the changes from reaching physical behavior.

In a separate demonstration, VicOne researchers provide a concrete example of a weakness affecting a protective function. The researchers exploited a vulnerability to prevent a robot’s remote-stop command from working. The case shows why teams need to test whether safeguards remain effective when the software supporting them is compromised.

Video 1. VicOne researchers demonstrate a vulnerability that prevents a robot’s remote-stop command from working. VicOne

AI can shorten the search for weaknesses, but a robotics team still needs to determine whether a fix is safe to deploy. Even after a software maintainer releases a patch, teams must identify affected systems, check compatibility, and verify that the update preserves intended behavior.

An earlier successful test remains useful evidence. However, a newly discovered weakness may reveal conditions that test never examined.

When immediate updating is impractical, teams may need temporary safeguards, such as restricting access to an affected service, while a validated fix is prepared.

As details from the 28 findings become available through coordinated disclosure, the next step is for robotics manufacturers is to connect each finding to its potential effect on development, deployment, and robot behavior.

That work also requires understanding how threats could affect robot behavior and how to protect systems already in operation. VicOne Radeis helps teams identify potential zero-day vulnerabilities, assess AI model and system security, and use simulation to evaluate how these risks could affect robot behavior before deployment. VicOne Rthena supports threat detection and responses within approved policies during operation.

Figure 2. Cybersecurity strengthens robot safety evidence throughout the lifecycle. VicOne helps teams test safety limits against manipulation before deployment and monitor the conditions behind safe behavior in operation.VicOne

Faster vulnerability discovery matters when teams can turn findings into action: identify what needs attention, verify that safeguards still hold, and confirm that a fix does not introduce new risks. That is how cybersecurity strengthens robot safety as systems continue to change.

For a deeper look how cybersecurity can affect robot safety, download our white paper, “Why Robot Safety Depends on Cybersecurity: Protecting the Information That Safety Decisions Rely On.”

VicOne is a Physical AI cybersecurity company protecting vehicles and robots from cyber threats that can alter behavior and compromise safety. Headquartered in Tokyo, Japan, the company provides automotive and robotics organizations with software and services to identify cyber risks early, assess their potential safety impact, and protect systems in operation, helping maintain safe, reliable behavior across real-world deployments.

#3159. These Are the Best Black Friday 2026 Deals on Kindles and E-Readers

Score the year's biggest savings during the Black Friday sale on the best e-reader deals as they launch in real time. Follow our Black Friday Live Blog for live coverage of the absolute best deals, flash sales, and tech savings. For a deep dive into top-rated offers, expert buying guides, and exclusive discounts, explore our Best Black Friday Amazon Tech Deals page.

Amazon's Black Friday sale is in full swing, which means it's a good time to score some of the year's best prices on e-readers. Timing your purchase is now a bigger deal than ever (so to speak), as Amazon recently raised the price of basically every Kindle by $50 or more due to the ongoing RAM crisis.

Because of this, the prices aren't nearly as low as they were last year, but now is still the time to get a decent discount on a Kindle Paperwhite or Colorsoft—but if you'd rather read differently, you can also save big on a few worthy Kindle alternatives. Here are your e-reader best bets in the lead-up to Black Friday and Cyber Monday.

The Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition is the best e-reader for most people. An upgraded version of the basic Kindle, the Paperwhite adds a larger screen, temperature-adjustable lighting, water resistance, and better battery life—and if you opt for the Signature Edition, you also get double the storage and no lock screen ads. Earlier this year, it jumped in price to $250, even before the company introduced a new model—but you can get the 2024 model for $179.99, 28% off the new list price.

If you want a great Kindle but you don't care about paying extra for more storage or getting rid of lock screen ads, the non-Signature Edition of the Kindle Paperwhite is also a great buy right now. The 2024 model has been discounted to $129.99 from the list price of $199.99. It's available in standard black, Jade, or Raspberry colors.

If you don't need the bells and whistles of the Paperwhite, you can also pick up the standard Kindle. It's still a very capable device, with good lighting, 16GB of onboard storage, and the ability to hook up your Bluetooth speakers to listen to Audible audiobooks. The standard Kindle, which now retails for $150, is marked down to $119.99, making it the cheapest Kindle option. Though I think it makes more sense to spend $10 more on the Signature Edition, this is the way to go if you want the cute Matcha color.

If you like to read comics or you just appreciate looking at your book covers in full color, the 2024 Kindle Colorsoft is also at a strong 41% discount for Black Friday, bringing it down to around $170. For $10 less than the Paperwhite Signature edition, you get all the same perks (including an ad-free experience) and a color e-ink screen that's great for reading magazines, graphic novels, and manga. Color e-ink isn't for everyone, but if it's for you, the Colorsoft has the best color screen on the market. For an extra $10, the Colorsoft Kids Edition adds a case, a yearlong subscription to Kindle Kids+, and an extended warranty.

If you're looking for a combination e-reader and e-notebook, the Kindle Scribe is a great option. With a larger screen than Amazon's other e-readers, it offers all the benefits of the Paperwhite but adds support for the excellent Premium Pen stylus, allowing you to take notes in your Amazon e-books or create handwritten documents that you can later convert to text using the onboard AI tools. The 32GB black-and-white version of the Kindle Scribe is currently $349.99, while the Colorsoft version will run you $449.99. Both of these are the newest models, released in 2025.

The new Kindle Scribe Colorsoft has all the same great features of the black-and-white version discussed above, but adds a full-color e-ink display. Combined with the large 11-inch screen, this makes it a great device for reading comics or magazine articles as they were meant to be read, or marking up PDFs using the included Premium Pen. This device usually costs a hefty $630, but the current Black Friday sale cuts $180 off of that price.

If you want to step outside of the Amazon ecosystem, the Kobo Libra Colour is a good bet. Discounted $30 to $229.99 at Best Buy, it's currently pricier than the Kindle Colorsoft, but you get a bit more for your money. While most of the specs are similar (they both use the same Kaleido 3 screen and offer 32GB of storage), the Kobo supports a stylus, so you can jot down notes in your books or keep a digital journal. It also has physical page-turn buttons, which the Colorsoft lacks.

If you don't want to be tied to the Amazon ecosystem and/or you're looking for a device that's a bit more portable, consider the Viwoods AiPaper Reader, currently marked down to $200, its lowest price ever. It's got a 6.13-inch screen, so it's the same size and shape as your phone, and it has a crisp e-ink screen with a strong (if not temperature-adjustable) front light and 128GB of onboard storage. #3157. Will Ferrell Comedy ‘The Hawk’ Canceled By Netflix After One Season

EXCLUSIVE: The Hawk did not make the cut for a second season. Netflix has opted not to renew the freshman golf comedy, co-created, executive produced and headlined by Will Ferrell. The news comes more than four months after The Hawk, SNL alum Ferrell’s first TV starring vehicle, premiered on July 16.

The decision fits Netflix’s performance vs. cost renewal criteria. The Hawk was believed to be among the most expensive comedy series on Netflix, with its star Ferrell commanding a seven-figure episodic salary. It spent three weeks in Netflix’s Global Top 10 for English series, peaking at No.2 with 6.2M views for its first full week, a respectable but not outsized delivery.

The show did not score well with critics, averaging 33% in reviews on Rotten Tomatoes but did better with core Will Ferrell fans for a 65% audience score. Watch on Deadline

The Hawk‘s fate was telegraphed by co-creator/executive producer Harper Steele during an interview on Late Night with Seth Meyers two weeks ago in which she said, in passing, “I was working on a short-lived but probably the best show ever, The Hawk.”

Ferrell remains in business with Netflix. Via Gloria Sanchez Productions, he executive produces the streamer’s upcoming series All the Rage, Prep as well as Nikki Glaser’s first scripted show, developed through Netflix Is a Joke Studios.

Of the comedy series that have released new seasons after The Hawk‘s debut, Netflix has renewed Nobody Wants This, whose third season delivered the biggest 2026 opening week for a returning scripted comedy, Tires and freshman A Different World. Leanne is awaiting word on a Season 3 pickup; it’s too early for Minimum Wage.

Upcoming Netflix comedy series also include Uncorked, A Hundred Percent and I Suck at Girls.

In The Hawk, Lonnie Hawkins (Ferrell), 2004’s number one golfer, struggles on the back nine of his career to recapture his magic. His body says retire, but his heart says he’s not done yet. His ex-wife and his son Lance, golf’s new golden boy, know he’s through. But with one more major to win to complete golf’s Grand Slam, Lonnie refuses to believe he’s anything other than one stroke away from the greatest comeback in golf history.

In the series, Ferrell reunited with former SNL co-star Molly Shannon who played his foul-mouthed ex-wife. Jimmy Tatro, Fortune Feimster, Luke Wilson, Chris Parnell, Katelyn Tarver and David Hornsby also starred in The Hawk, which was co-created by Ferrell, Steele and Chris Henchy.

Ferrell, Jessica Elbaum and Alix Taylor executive produced for Gloria Sanchez Productions. Rian Johnson, Ram Bergman and Nena Rodrigue were executive producers for T-Street. Henchy, Steele, David Gordon Green and Andrew Guest also executive produced.

#3156. Advanced Metrology for Defect Detection, Tool Health, and Semiconductor Yield Enhancement



In advanced semiconductor manufacturing, small defects can have a large effect on yield. Thin film deposition tools must stay stable and qualified. Process drift must be caught early. When a defect does appear, engineers need to know where it came from and how it affects device performance. This webinar shows how in-line inspection and offline characterization combine into one workflow, from tool monitoring to root-cause analysis.

In the first half, Dr. Bitan Chakraborty from Intel, explains how surface scan metrology fits into station monitors for thin film tools. The session shows how baseline signatures and real-time monitoring reveal hardware wear, particle generation, and process drift before they reach production wafers. It then moves to in-line scans on patterned wafers. These scans expose layer-level defects and show how they form and spread through multi-layer device stacks. Linking this defect data to electrical test results helps teams find root causes and focus their yield improvement work.

In the second half, Dr. Jacob Petersen from Evident Scientific, addresses a common question: what happens after an in-line tool flags a problem? In-line tools are fast, but they cannot always provide the details needed for a firm conclusion. Offline 3D optical profilometry fills that gap by combining three complementary inspection techniques in a single system. It delivers dimensional measurements and helps determine whether a defect lies within the sample or comes from foreign material. The session covers how several optical techniques support inspection from bare silicon to fully packaged chips. It also shows how automation enables fast measurement of features down to the sub-nanometer scale with minimal operator handling.

What You Will Learn:

  • How surface scan metrology in station monitors tracks tool health and supports the qualification of thin film deposition processes
  • How baseline signatures and real-time monitoring detect particle generation, hardware degradation, and process drift before production is affected
  • How in-line scans on patterned wafers reveal layer-level defects and show how they propagate through multi-layer device structures
  • When offline 3D optical profilometry should follow in-line inspection, and how it measures dimensions and separates sample defects from foreign material
  • How correlating tool health data, inspection results, and electrical performance links physical defects to yield loss and guides targeted improvement projects

At Tom's Guide we use a diverse panel of sleep experts to test the most popular mattresses you can find online. We combine repeatable, scientific lab measurements with extended at-home sleep trials. Their review process is also editorially independent and free from brand influence.

Rather than relying solely on first impressions, we use standardized, objective lab tests to generate reliable, unbiased data. For instance, we use thermal imaging camera tests to see how well a mattress regulates temperature, and use accelerometers to test how well a mattress isolates motion.

Lab numbers do not tell the whole story, so a lead reviewer sleeps on each mattress at home for at least three weeks — the typical time it takes for a person's body to adjust to a new bed. We also gather feedback from a testing panel made up of people with different body types and sleeping positions to account for subjective comfort

You can find out more about how we test mattresses in our mattresses by reading up on our mattress methodology.

What does the "best mattress deals" mean?

Before I delve into each of the best Black Friday mattress deals, I want to start by clarifying what I mean by the "best mattress deals".

I consider the best mattress deals to A) feature a mattress that was awarded three stars or above by our expert team or online customers and B) meet at least one of the following criteria:

1. It isn't the usual discount — it's better. For example, a mattress that is usually 20% in the regular monthly mattress sales suddenly dropping to 30% off during the Black Friday period.

2. It's the usual discount, but with a free gift as a Black Friday bonus. For instance, a mattress stuck at the usual price, but with a free gift (such as a bedding bundle or gift card) worth $50 or more.

3. It's the usual discount, but still outstanding value for money. For example, a mattress in a price tier that's beneath its actual performance (such as a luxury mattress regularly sold at a mid-range price).

Welcome to our official 2026 Black Friday mattress deals live blog!

Frances Daniels, Senior Sleep Staff Writer

#3154. iOS 27.2 upgraded Apple Photos in two ways, here’s what’s new

Apple Photos got a lot of new features in iOS 27, but the recent release of iOS 27.2 brought even more improvements. Here’s what’s new.

Shared Albums are among my favorite features in the Photos app. I don’t post on social media often, but I love using Shared Albums because they provide a social media-style experience in a private way that lives right inside Photos.

iOS 27 brought a variety of big improvements to Shared Albums. And in iOS 27.2, Apple introduced four more.

Per Apple’s release notes, here’s what’s new:

To get these new features, you’ll need to make sure your Shared Albums have been upgraded for iOS 27.

One complication introduced by AI is that it can be hard to know if an image is real or AI-generated.

This challenge extends to AI-edited photos too, which might have key details changed by tools like iOS 27’s Extend, Reframe, and Clean Up features in Photos.

Apple is tackling the issue with its new Reference Image feature in iPhone 18 Pro, and also through a software enhancement that rolled out in iOS 27.2.

Per Apple, its latest software update adds the following:

Support for SynthID watermarking to help identify whether an image was generated or modified with generative tools in Photos and Image Playground

SynthID is a cross-platform standard developed by Google that embeds unnoticeable digital watermarks into AI-modified photos. Users won’t see a visible watermark, but anyone who checks for a SynthID marker will find it.

What do you think of the latest Apple Photos changes in iOS 27.2? Let us know in the comments.
